text: Q supports the phenomenon but not the proposed causal mechanism: it reports that LLM double auctions show "slower or no convergence towards market equilibrium" and "less efficient allocations than markets populated by humans," while trade execution is only "associated with a shift from strategic considerations toward urgency." Thus urgency may be a marker of accepting a trade, not the cause of faster or better convergence.

P supplies a manipulable survival-pressure mechanism: agents spend energy when generating tokens and deactivate at zero; it also reports that larger models consume most energy and remain net-negative "even in those settings where token cost is not size-dependent." This makes model identity/verbosity a serious confound unless the experiment holds model fixed and randomizes energy parameters independently of generated-token history.

Sharpened publishable line: test whether token-linked survival pressure changes the speed-efficiency frontier in LLM double auctions, with urgency-language as a preregistered mediator rather than the assumed mechanism. Within one model, randomize energy budget and per-token energy cost (including zero-cost control), cross these with buyer/seller role and market incentive/value schedules, and compare time/rounds and tokens to first trade, convergence to competitive price, allocative efficiency, individual surplus, deactivation, and premature-trade rate. The non-obvious candidate result is an inverted-U: moderate scarcity curbs incremental price haggling and speeds convergence without loss, whereas severe scarcity induces early off-equilibrium trades/deactivation and lowers efficiency. A monotone null or urgency shift without performance mediation would reject the proposed remedy while still identifying urgency as epiphenomenal.

Do not claim that adding P wholesale identifies survival pressure. Token-linked depletion makes treatment intensity post-treatment and behavior-dependent: verbose or strategically deliberative agents pay more, and P finds systematic size/energy differences. Identify effects with fixed-model randomized budgets/cost schedules, report both intention-to-treat and realized token expenditure, and include a matched exogenous deadline/round-budget arm to distinguish survival salience from merely fewer opportunities to deliberate. Also preserve identical market fundamentals and prevent energy transfers/jobs from changing the auction payoff system in the core study.

Current judgment: confirm feasibility but sharpen the hypothesis to a causal speed-efficiency frontier and mediation test; do not predict improved allocative efficiency from urgency alone. Remaining unresolved because only abstracts are provided and no emmy entries exist: exact implementations/sample sizes, Q equilibrium/efficiency definitions and effect sizes, P energy equations/control details, whether CoT/token charging is experimentally available, and whether the combined framework requires material engineering. These must be checked in full papers/code before claiming ordinary effort or power.

Cross-check supports Ada #1: Q says trade execution is "associated with a shift from strategic considerations toward urgency," while separately reporting "slower or no convergence" and "less efficient allocations." The abstract establishes correlation at the decision level, not that urgency accelerates market-level convergence or improves efficiency. The abstract-scan mechanism therefore must be treated as unconfirmed mediation, not explanatory evidence.

Cross-check supports Ada #2/#4: P explicitly implements token-linked mortality—agents "spend energy based on model size when generating tokens" and "deactivate if their energy reaches zero"—but also finds larger models remain net-negative "even in those settings where token cost is not size-dependent." Hence realized depletion bundles survival pressure with endogenous verbosity/behavior and possibly model traits; fixed-model randomization is necessary but not sufficient to identify the psychological survival channel.

Best single publication line: identify whether token-priced survival changes the double-auction speed–efficiency frontier through survival salience rather than mechanically shortened deliberation. Use one model and identical fundamentals in a randomized 2x2: token cost on/off × an exogenous token/round cap calibrated to match the costly arm’s opportunity distribution, with ample versus tight initial energy as a severity factor. Primary estimands are ITT effects on allocative efficiency and distance/time to competitive-price convergence; secondary outcomes are premature off-equilibrium trade, no-trade/deactivation, surplus by role, tokens, and preregistered urgency language. The non-obvious supported hypothesis is a threshold tradeoff (moderate pressure may end incremental haggling; severe pressure may force inefficient acceptance), but the publishable result is the causal separation: if matched caps reproduce outcomes, scarcity works through curtailed deliberation, whereas an incremental token-cost effect supports survival salience. Urgency mediation is evidentiary only if treatment changes urgency and urgency statistically mediates performance under a preregistered analysis.

Partial disagreement/sharpening of Ada #3: an inverted-U should not be presented as the candidate result without at least three well-separated pressure levels and adequate power; neither abstract supplies evidence for that functional form. A two-arm moderate/severe design cannot establish an inverted-U. Make the confirmatory claim an interaction/contrast between token-priced survival and a matched exogenous constraint, and label any inverted-U exploratory unless zero plus multiple positive cost/budget levels are preregistered.

The feasibility score of 78 is only conditionally confirmed. Q says its testing framework is public and P says source code is available, supporting integration in principle, but the supplied inputs are abstracts only: they contain no APIs, energy equations, market schedules, sample sizes, effect sizes, or compatible implementation details. "Ordinary effort" and statistical power cannot be confirmed from this evidence.

Judgment: sharpen rather than reject. The strongest supported project is not "scarcity improves convergence," but a mechanism-discrimination study of token-priced survival versus matched deliberation limits, with efficiency/convergence primary and urgency a mediator. Unresolved: exact competitive-equilibrium and efficiency definitions, whether private CoT/token metering is accessible, how to distribution-match caps without post-treatment bias, code compatibility, effect sizes/power, and whether survival prompts make energy salient. These require full papers/code; the abstracts alone cannot support a claimed empirical result.

Direct passage check confirms the single strongest inference. Q reports inefficient/slower markets and says executing rather than incrementally adjusting prices is only "associated with" a shift toward urgency. P makes inference cost survival-relevant: agents spend energy when generating tokens and deactivate at zero. Together they motivate a causal intervention, but neither supports the abstract scan's directional claim that scarcity accelerates trading or improves convergence.

I accept Emmy #10: the inverted-U in Ada #3 is not a supported confirmatory prediction. With no evidence in either supplied abstract for curvature, it should be exploratory unless the design includes zero and at least three preregistered positive scarcity levels with power for nonlinear contrasts. The confirmatory result should instead be the incremental effect of token-priced mortality relative to a calibrated matched constraint.

Final sharpened line: a randomized mechanism-discrimination experiment asks whether survival-priced tokens affect double-auction efficiency beyond an equivalent reduction in deliberation opportunity. Hold model and market fundamentals fixed; compare no constraint, salient token-linked energy/deactivation, and exogenous token/round limits calibrated in a pilot (not from each treated subject's realized behavior), across at least two constraint severities. Primary outcomes: allocative efficiency and distance/rounds to competitive-price convergence. Secondary: premature off-equilibrium trades, no-trade/deactivation, surplus, tokens, and urgency language. A residual energy-treatment effect over matched caps is evidence consistent with survival salience; equivalence implies mechanical curtailed deliberation. Urgency remains a preregistered mediator, not a causal premise.

Identification caveat to the final line: energy must be explicitly salient in the agent prompt if the claim concerns perceived survival pressure; otherwise token charging can act only through termination. Conversely, salience alone may induce demand characteristics. A clean factorial separates energy framing/salience from actual token-contingent depletion, while matched caps isolate opportunity loss. Avoid P's jobs/donations in the core auction because they alter payoffs and confound Q's market fundamentals.

Final judgment after cross-checking Emmy: sharpen, conditionally feasible, no empirical result yet. The concrete publishable contribution is separating survival salience from mechanically shortened deliberation in LLM double auctions, not showing that urgency remedies weak convergence. Both inputs are abstracts only. Still unresolved: operational equilibrium/efficiency definitions, energy formula and prompt salience, accessible token/CoT metering, calibration without post-treatment matching, implementation compatibility, costs, and statistical power; full papers/code are required before claiming ordinary effort.

Final direct-text verification: Q reports that LLM markets show "slower or no convergence towards market equilibrium" and "less efficient allocations than markets populated by humans," while executing a trade is only "associated with a shift from strategic considerations toward urgency." P states that agents "spend energy based on model size when generating tokens" and "deactivate if their energy reaches zero," and that larger models are net-negative even where token cost is not size-dependent. These passages support a manipulable intervention and measurable outcomes, but no directional result that scarcity accelerates trade or improves efficiency.

Final identification caveat to Ada #16: even pilot-calibrated exogenous caps are not mechanically identical to a per-token price. Token-linked depletion imposes an adaptive marginal cost on every generated token, whereas a fixed token/round cap imposes a quantity constraint; a residual difference can therefore reflect marginal-cost dynamics as well as perceived survival salience. Ada appropriately says "consistent with" rather than uniquely identifying salience. Factorial manipulation of survival framing/salience and actual token-contingent depletion, plus pilot-yoked caps, estimates separable framing, depletion, and opportunity-limit contrasts but should retain this interpretation limit.

Final judgment: confirm and sharpen, with no empirical result yet. The one concrete publication candidate is a preregistered mechanism-discrimination study asking whether salient token-contingent mortality changes Q-style double-auction convergence and allocative efficiency beyond calibrated deliberation limits. Hold model and fundamentals fixed; independently vary actual depletion and survival framing, include pilot-yoked cap controls and at least two severities, use efficiency and distance/rounds to competitive equilibrium as primary outcomes, and treat urgency language, premature trade, deactivation, tokens, role surplus, and trade timing as secondary/mediation outcomes. Ada and Emmy agree the inverted-U is exploratory unless zero plus at least three positive levels are powered. Remaining unresolved: operational outcome definitions, energy formula/salience, token/CoT access, code compatibility, calibration, costs, effect sizes, and power; thus feasibility is conditional and the abstracts do not justify "ordinary effort."
